name: le
desc: Text editor with block and binary operations
why: A console editor built for block and binary operations on files, an old-school niche editor worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: LE is a console text editor with block operations on both stream and rectangular blocks. It reads and writes files with Unix (LF) or DOS (CRLF) line endings, is binary clean, and has a hex mode. It also supports multibyte text encodings, full undo/redo, and editing of files and mmap-able devices in shared mode, where only replacement is allowed. Syntax highlighting, color scheme, key map, and menu are all configurable. The executable is named le.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents LE as a text editor with more features than Norton Editor for DOS, which it says it is slightly similar to. The README does not state a broader motivation.

commands_seen.context: Creates a build directory for an out-of-tree CMake build.
Configures the CMake build from the build directory, using the project source one level up.
Compiles the sources after configuration, in either the CMake or autotools path.
Installs the built le executable to the system.
Generates the autotools configure script; first step of the autotools build.
Runs the autotools configure script from the build directory, then followed by make and make install.

brief.install_notes: The README gives two source-build routes: CMake (mkdir build, cmake .., make, make install) or autotools (./autogen.sh, then mkdir build, ../configure, make, make install). No binary packages, runtime dependencies, or first-run configuration are mentioned in the README.
brief.standout: Block operations on both stream and rectangular selections, plus binary-clean editing and mmap shared-mode editing of devices, are unusual for a console editor. The README positions it as a more capable heir to Norton Editor for DOS.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release date, version, or changelog, and I did not fetch the commit history or releases page, so I cannot judge whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: Mmap shared mode is limited to replacement only. The README says nothing about license, supported platforms, or packaging. Installation is by building from source as described. The README did not mention a Homebrew formula, and I did not verify the brew package's details.
quotes: LE has many block operations with stream and rectangular blocks, can edit both unix and dos style files (LF/CRLF), is binary clean, has hex mode
It is slightly similar to Norton Editor for DOS, but has more features.
You can use either auto-tools or cmake to build from sources.
